mainTopic: When unfinished vessels and bone vessels can become טמא; the stages when almonds are obligated in tithes; and the status of תמד before and after fermenting
overview: The amud opens at the end of a list of finishing jobs for metal vessels. Until those jobs are done, a metal vessel cannot become טמא. The גמרא asks why metal is stricter than wood. רבי יוחנן says metal vessels are made for honor, and רב נחמן says they are expensive. The two reasons split on כלי עצם (bone vessels), and a ברייתא on "וכל מעשה עזים" proves that vessels made from animal horns and hooves can become טמא, but those made from birds cannot. A new משנה then teaches that bitter and sweet almonds are obligated in תרומה ומעשרות at opposite stages, depending on when each one is fit to eat. Next, a משנה teaches that תמד counts as water before it ferments and as wine after. It also teaches that brothers who are partners pay either the קלבון or מעשר בהמה, never both. The גמרא asks whose view the תמד ruling follows, since it seems to fit neither the רבנן nor רבי יהודה, and רב נחמן's answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: The last finishing steps for metal vessels
steps.stepSummary: The source finishes its list of finishing steps for metal vessels. A metal vessel missing a base, rim or handle cannot become טמא, but one missing only a cover can.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner still plans to smooth it, set ornaments in it, plane it, decorate it, or hammer it, it is not yet a finished vessel. If it is missing a base, a rim or a handle, it is טהור (it cannot become טמא). If it is only missing a cover, it can become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a teaching about when a metal vessel counts as finished, so that it can become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As long as one of these finishing jobs is still planned, the metal vessel is not yet a real vessel for טומאה. A missing base, rim or handle means the vessel itself is not complete. A cover is a separate item, so the vessel is already complete without it.

keyTerms.meaning: To set ornaments or gems into it
Here: cannot become impure / can become impure

steps.confusionAlert: Here טהור does not mean the vessel was made pure. It means the vessel cannot become טמא yet, because it is not finished.

phrases.english: To smooth, to set in ornaments, to plane,
to decorate, to strike with a hammer.

phrases.aramaic: מְחוּסָּר כַּן אוֹ אוֹגֶן אוֹ אוֹזֶן – טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: If it is missing a base, or a rim, or a handle, it is pure (it cannot become impure),
if it is missing a cover, it is impure (it can become impure).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the teaching about when vessels become finished, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A metal vessel cannot become טמא until every planned finishing step is done. A missing cover does not stop it from being finished.

steps.title: Why are metal and wooden vessels treated differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why unfinished wooden vessels can become טמא once usable, while metal vessels must be completely finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about these (wooden vessels), and what is different about those (metal vessels)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the two kinds of vessels follow different rules and asks for the reason. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wooden vessel can become טמא as soon as it is usable, even if it is not polished. A metal vessel must be fully finished first. The גמרא wants to know what makes metal different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks for the reason behind a different rule

phrases.english: What is different about these
phrases.notes: "These" are the wooden vessels mentioned earlier, which can become impure once they are usable.

phrases.english: and what is different about those?
phrases.notes: "Those" are the metal vessels, which must be completely finished first.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the metal-vessel rule just stated, compared with the earlier wooden-vessel rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason metal vessels need full completion before they can become טמא, while wooden vessels do not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: metal vessels are made for honor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that metal vessels are made for honor and display, so they do not count as vessels until they are fully finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Since they (metal vessels) are made for honor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first answer: metal vessels are meant to look fine, so a half-finished one is not yet what it is meant to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A metal vessel's purpose includes looking honorable. If it still needs polishing or decorating, it has not reached its purpose. That is why it is not yet a vessel for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: They are made for honor or display

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Since they are made for honor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הוֹאִיל וּלְכָבוֹד עֲשׂוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Metal vessels are made for honor, so they are not real vessels until they are fully finished.

steps.title: רב נחמן: metal vessels are expensive
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives a different reason: metal vessels are costly, so no one considers them done until they are complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Since their price is expensive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן offers a second, different answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because metal vessels cost a lot, an unfinished one cannot be sold at full value. So people do not treat it as a finished vessel until it is complete. His reason is about money, not about honor.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Since their price is expensive.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: הוֹאִיל וּדְמֵיהֶן יְקָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question that רבי יוחנן answered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Metal vessels are expensive, so they are not considered vessels until they are complete.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in which case the two reasons would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to different results. This sets up the case of bone vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons explain metal vessels equally well. So the גמרא looks for a case where one reason applies and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers given in steps 3 and 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רבי יוחנן's reason and רב נחמן's reason give different rulings.

steps.title: The difference is bone vessels
steps.stepSummary: The two opinions differ about כלי עצם, vessels made of bone or horn, which are expensive but not made for honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is bone vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that bone vessels are where the two reasons split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bone vessels are costly but are not used for display. According to רב נחמן (cost), they must be fully finished, like metal. According to רבי יוחנן (honor), they are like wood and can become טמא once usable.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels made from bone, such as horn
There is a difference between them

phrases.english: The difference between them is bone vessels,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bone vessels: expensive but not made for honor.

steps.title: רב נחמן is consistent: bone vessels are like metal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב נחמן said elsewhere that bone vessels are like metal vessels, which matches his reason here.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן follows his own reasoning, as רב נחמן said: Bone vessels are like metal vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the difference it just gave by pointing to another statement of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן elsewhere puts bone vessels in the same group as metal vessels. That fits his idea that being expensive is what matters. So we see he really does hold that bone vessels must be fully finished.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own line of reasoning
They are similar, they have the same status

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: metal needs full finishing because it is made for honor. רב נחמן: because it is expensive. So for רב נחמן, bone vessels (expensive) are like metal.

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman follows his own reasoning,
as Rav Naḥman said:
Bone vessels are like metal vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 6 with another statement of רב נחמן.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רב נחמן, bone vessels follow the metal-vessel rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's own statement: כלי עצם ככלי מתכות דמו.

steps.title: Can bone vessels become טמא at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that this discussion assumes bone vessels can become טמא, and asks if that is really so.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that bone vessels can become impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check a hidden assumption. Arguing about when bone vessels become טמא only makes sense if they can become טמא at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists specific materials that can become טמא, and bone is not clearly one of them. So the גמרא needs a source showing that bone vessels can become טמא.

phrases.english: Does this imply that bone vessels can become impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions an assumption behind steps 6 and 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether bone vessels can become טמא at all, and what the source is.

steps.title: Yes: the פסוק includes items made from goat horns and hooves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says yes and quotes a ברייתא in which רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה reads "וכל מעשה עזים" as including vessels made from goat horns and hooves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as it was taught: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: Why does the פסוק say "and all work of goats you shall purify"? To include things that come from goats: from the horns and from the hooves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes and brings a ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק needed to mention "work of goats." It answers that the words come to include items made from goat horns and hooves. These are bone-type materials, so they can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק say this? It asks what an extra word comes to teach
You shall purify. This shows these items can become impure

phrases.english: Yes, as it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:
What does the verse come to teach when it says
"And all work of goats you shall purify"?
To include something that comes from goats,
from the horns and from the hooves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The פסוק "וכל מעשה עזים" includes vessels made from goat horns and hooves.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה on במדבר 31:20.

steps.title: The word "all" extends this to every animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that horns and hooves of other animals are included too, and answers from the word "וכל" (and all).
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know other domesticated and wild animals? The פסוק says "and all work."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא widens the rule from goats to all animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "all" is read as a word that widens the rule. So vessels made from the horns and hooves of any animal, domesticated or wild, can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: And all. Read as a word that widens the rule

phrases.english: From where do we know other domesticated and wild animals?
The verse says: "And all work."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא, widening the rule beyond goats.
steps.raayaObject: That vessels from the horns and hooves of all animals can become טמא.

steps.title: "Goats" comes to exclude birds
steps.stepSummary: If "all" includes every animal, the word "goats" seems unneeded. The ברייתא answers that it comes to exclude birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say "goats"? To exclude birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the word "goats" is still needed: to exclude vessels made from birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Goats are animals, not birds. So naming goats limits the rule to animals like them, and bird bones are left out. This finishes the proof that animal bone vessels can become טמא, which answers the question of step 8.
steps.whatToRemember: Vessels made from the horns and hooves (bone) of any animal can become טמא, learned from "וכל מעשה עזים." Vessels made from birds cannot.

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say "goats"?
To exclude birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by explaining the word "goats" once "all" has widened the rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Bone vessels from animals can become טמא. Vessels from birds cannot. This confirms the assumption behind the dispute between רבי יוחנן and רב נחמן.

steps.title: New משנה: Bitter and sweet almonds are opposites
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that whatever stage makes bitter almonds obligated makes sweet almonds exempt, and the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The stage when bitter almonds are obligated is the stage when sweet almonds are exempt. The stage when sweet almonds are obligated is the stage when bitter almonds are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the bone-vessels discussion and opens a brand-new משנה about almonds. It does not yet say which stage is which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obligation in view is separating תרומה ומעשרות, which applies only to food fit to eat. The משנה says bitter and sweet almonds work in opposite ways, but it leaves out the details. The next step will fill them in.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the text the גמרא now explains
Obligated / exempt (here, in separating תרומה ומעשרות)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic and has nothing to do with the bone vessels in the previous steps. The משנה never mentions תרומה ומעשרות, but that is the obligation it means.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The stage that is obligated in bitter almonds is exempt in sweet ones,
phrases.notes: Obligated in separating תרומה ומעשרות. The משנה leaves this unsaid.

phrases.english: and the stage that is obligated in sweet ones is exempt in bitter ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the bone-vessels sugya
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bitter and sweet almonds have opposite stages of obligation for תרומה ומעשרות.

steps.title: ברייתא explains which almonds are obligated
steps.stepSummary: Small bitter almonds and large sweet almonds are obligated. Large bitter almonds and small sweet almonds are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bitter almonds: small ones are obligated, large ones are exempt. Sweet almonds: large ones are obligated, small ones are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא spells out the details the משנה left vague. It tells us which size of each kind of almond is obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule follows whether the almond is edible. A bitter almond is still edible while small, but it becomes bitter as it grows. A sweet almond becomes good to eat only once it is large and ripe.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
Bitter almonds: small ones are obligated,
phrases.notes: While they are small, they are not bitter yet and can be eaten.

phrases.english: large ones are exempt.
Sweet almonds: large ones are obligated,
small ones are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה in detail
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Edibility decides: small bitter almonds and large sweet almonds are obligated.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's view: all bitter almonds are treated alike
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי quotes his father as treating small and large bitter almonds the same. The ברייתא reports two versions: all are exempt, or all are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי says in his father's name that both small and large bitter almonds are exempt. Some report that he said both are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion disagrees with the ברייתא about bitter almonds. It says size makes no difference, but people disagree about how this opinion was reported.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא split bitter almonds by size. רבי יוסי treats all bitter almonds the same way. In one version he exempts them all, and in the other he obligates them all.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both the small and the large

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei says in the name of his father:
both this and that are exempt,
phrases.notes: Both small and large bitter almonds.

phrases.english: and some say: both this and that are obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting view on bitter almonds
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bitter almonds of every size are treated alike, either all exempt or all obligated.

steps.title: רבי חנינא ruled that all bitter almonds are exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעא reports that רבי חנינא ruled in ציפורי that both small and large bitter almonds are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעא said: רבי חנינא ruled in ציפורי according to the one who says both are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: We learn how the matter was ruled in practice. רבי חנינא followed the version that exempts all bitter almonds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the two reported versions, this tells us which one was actually followed. רבי חנינא, ruling in ציפורי, exempted bitter almonds of every size.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows which version was followed as practical הלכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ela said:
Rabbi Chanina issued a ruling in Tzippori
according to the one who says both this and that are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports which version was followed in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, both small and large bitter almonds are exempt.

steps.title: How can large bitter almonds be obligated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what use large bitter almonds have, according to the view that obligates them.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says both are obligated, what are the large ones good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the second version, which obligates all bitter almonds. Large bitter almonds seem inedible, so why would anyone need to separate תרומה ומעשרות from them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food that cannot be eaten is not obligated in תרומה ומעשרות. Large bitter almonds are too bitter to eat, so obligating them seems wrong. The גמרא wants to know how this view makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: And according to the one who says both this and that are obligated,
what are the large ones fit for?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר זֶה וָזֶה לְחִיּוּב, גְּדוֹלִים לְמַאי חֲזוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the obligating version from step 14 and questions its logic
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way are large bitter almonds edible, so that they could be obligated?

steps.title: They can be sweetened by fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that large bitter almonds count as food because roasting them over fire can sweeten them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: since one can sweeten them by means of fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. Large bitter almonds can be made edible by roasting, so they count as food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food does not have to be edible raw. If it can easily be made edible, it still counts as food. That is why the obligating view treats large bitter almonds as obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: By means of fire, such as roasting

steps.whatToRemember: Small bitter almonds and large sweet almonds are edible, so they are obligated. One view exempts all bitter almonds, and רבי חנינא ruled that way. The view that obligates all of them reasons that large bitter almonds can be sweetened by fire.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְיָכוֹל לְמַתְּקָן עַל יְדֵי הָאוּר.
phrases.english: Since one can sweeten them by means of fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְיָכוֹל לְמַתְּקָן עַל יְדֵי הָאוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Large bitter almonds count as food because roasting can sweeten them.

steps.title: The משנה on תמד before and after fermenting
steps.stepSummary: Unfermented תמד cannot be bought with מעשר money and disqualifies a מקוה. Fermented תמד can be bought with מעשר money and does not disqualify a מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: תמד that has not yet fermented may not be bought with מעשר money, and it disqualifies a מקוה. Once it has fermented, it may be bought with מעשר money, and it does not disqualify a מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with the law of תמד, a weak drink made by soaking leftover grape skins in water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fermenting is the dividing line. Before fermenting, תמד is treated like water: it is not food you can buy with מעשר שני money, and it acts like drawn water that ruins a מקוה. After fermenting it counts as wine, so both rulings reverse.

keyTerms.meaning: A drink made by soaking leftover grape skins and seeds in water
מעשר שני money, which may only be spent on food and drink in ירושלים

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא's question in the next steps is built entirely on this fermenting line.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Temed, before it has fermented –
may not be bought with tithe money,
phrases.notes: This is מעשר שני money. You may only spend it on real food or drink, and plain water doesn't count.

phrases.english: and it disqualifies the ritual bath.
phrases.notes: At this stage it counts like drawn water, and enough drawn water falling in ruins a מקוה.

phrases.english: Once it has fermented – it may be bought with tithe money,
and it does not disqualify the ritual bath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of bitter almonds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unfermented תמד has the status of water. Fermented תמד has the status of wine.

steps.title: Brothers who are partners: the premium or animal tithe
steps.stepSummary: Brothers who are partners pay either the קלבון or מעשר בהמה, never both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Brothers who are partners: when they must pay the קלבון, they are exempt from מעשר בהמה. When they must give מעשר בהמה, they are exempt from the קלבון.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second, separate ruling about brothers who inherited together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two duties exclude each other. If the brothers are treated as partners, they pay the קלבון (an extra fee added to the מחצית השקל) and are exempt from מעשר בהמה. If the estate is still treated as one shared property, they owe מעשר בהמה and not the קלבון.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers who are partners in an inheritance
A small extra fee added to the half-shekel payment
The tithe of animals, taken from every tenth newborn animal

phrases.english: Brothers who are partners,
when they are obligated in the premium –
they are exempt from animal tithe;
when they are obligated in animal tithe –
they are exempt from the premium.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent ruling in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קלבון and מעשר בהמה exclude each other for brothers who are partners.

steps.title: Whose view is the משנה? It seems to fit neither side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the תמד ruling follows. It cites a dispute in which the רבנן exempt תמד that yields only its water and רבי יהודה obligates it.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Whose view is our משנה? It seems to be neither רבי יהודה nor the רבנן. For it was taught: if someone makes תמד, puts in a measured amount of water, and finds that he ends up with only that same amount, he is exempt. רבי יהודה obligates him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the תמד ruling and asks which תנא it follows. It brings a source showing a dispute that does not seem to match the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the cited source, the רבנן look at quantity: if nothing came out beyond the water put in, it is only water and is exempt from מעשר. רבי יהודה looks at taste: it tastes like wine, so it must be tithed. Our משנה instead uses fermenting as the test, which neither of these views mentions.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does our משנה follow?
One who makes תמד by pouring water over grape leftovers

phrases.english: GEMARA: Whose view is our Mishnah?
Not Rabbi Yehuda and not the Rabbis,
as it was taught: one who makes temed
and put in water by measure
and found just his measure – is exempt,
phrases.notes: He is exempt from מעשר, because nothing came out except the water he put in.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda obligates.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין? לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the תמד ruling in step 18 and tests it against a known dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fermenting test in the משנה's תמד ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The known dispute uses quantity or taste as the test, not fermenting, so the משנה seems to match no one.

steps.title: Spelling out why neither side fits
steps.stepSummary: Under the רבנן, תמד should be exempt even after fermenting. Under רבי יהודה, it should be obligated even before fermenting. רב נחמן begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? If the רבנן, then it should be exempt even if it fermented. If רבי יהודה, it should be obligated even if it did not ferment. רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens its question by showing how each side clashes with the משנה. Then it sets up an answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, fermenting changes nothing, because the amount is still just the original water. For רבי יהודה, the wine taste is enough even before fermenting. Either way, the משנה's split at the point of fermenting does not fit, so רב נחמן steps in to resolve it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two tests: the רבנן go by how much liquid came out, and רבי יהודה goes by taste. Neither one goes by fermenting, and that is the whole problem.

phrases.english: Whose view is it?

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבָּנַן – אַף עַל גַּב דְּהֶחְמִיץ,
phrases.english: If the Rabbis – even if it fermented,
phrases.notes: The גמרא means it should still be treated as plain water, even after it ferments.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא הֶחְמִיץ!
phrases.english: If Rabbi Yehuda – even if it did not ferment!
phrases.notes: For him, the wine taste is enough, even before it ferments.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
phrases.notes: This line opens the answer. The answer itself comes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִי רַבָּנַן – אַף עַל גַּב דְּהֶחְמִיץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the problem raised in step 20 and introduces the speaker who will answer it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Matching the משנה to either the רבנן or רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן would exempt תמד even after fermenting, and רבי יהודה would obligate it even before, so the משנה's fermenting split fits neither.
